title: Symplectic and contact geometry
summary: A geometric complement to the existing symplectic and Floer foundations: construct contact and Reeb geometry with its genuine differential data, prove contact and Lagrangian neighbourhood theorems, develop Hamiltonian actions and regular symplectic reduction, and establish torus convexity and Delzant classification with fixed signs, periods, lattices and moment-map normalizations. Existing bilinear, smooth-manifold and Lie-group theories are reused.
readme:
# Symplectic and contact geometry

This roadmap develops the contact and Hamiltonian geometric landscape surrounding the existing analytic Heegaard Floer programme. It imports that programme's symplectic manifolds, Darboux-Moser and exact Floer foundations rather than constructing parallel objects. Its endpoints are contact and symplectic neighbourhood comparisons, regular reduction, convexity and Delzant's equivariant symplectic classification. Generic smooth manifolds and tubular neighbourhoods remain with GeometricTopology; the Lie algebra, exponential and adjoint representations remain with LieGroups.

The pointwise contact layer uses existing real vector spaces, duals, bilinear forms and TauCeti.SymplecticForm. On a manifold its inputs must be alpha and the ACTUAL d alpha. Smoothness, derivative identities and global flows are separate proof obligations. A manifold is a type with Mathlib instances, not a bespoke bundled replacement.

Conventions: the contact form is selected and cooriented; its Reeb field satisfies alpha(R)=1 and contraction of d alpha with R is zero. A positive function preserves that coorientation, but its Reeb field is not generally R/f. Use alpha_std=dz-sum p_i dq_i, omega_can=-d lambda_can, and symplectization d(exp(t)alpha). Hamiltonian fields satisfy contraction of omega with X_H=dH. For left actions use exp(t xi) acting on x and coadjoint action by the dual of Ad_(g inverse). The torus is R^n/(2 pi Z^n), so the standard circle moment on C is -|z|^2/2. Moment-map translations and integral torus reidentifications are never suppressed in the classification.

Scope boundaries: cooriented contact geometry in finite dimension; compact/support or completeness hypotheses where a flow must be global; compact free regular reduction yielding manifolds. Noncooriented line-bundle contact geometry, singular/orbifold reduction and virtual contact/Floer theories are not endpoints of this design. Their omission does not weaken the stated regular theorems. Holomorphic curves, Maslov theory and exact Lagrangian Floer complexes are imported from HeegaardFloer, not duplicated.

The declaration packet supplies the pointwise contact prefix and records precise smooth/global proof leaves. The detailed companion reader is authoritative; no stage or signature is asserted implemented.

## SC.0: Pointwise contact and Reeb geometry

Construct the contact predicate on actual covectors and alternating bilinear forms, the horizontal symplectic restriction, the normalized Reeb vector and its splitting. Use the existing finite-dimensional bilinear dual equivalence. Retain the derivative term in first-order rescaling and prove its horizontal Reeb correction. Construct the pointwise form beneath symplectization. This is not a smooth-manifold construction.

## SC.1: Smooth contact forms and Reeb dynamics

Identify the pointwise pair with a smooth form and its actual exterior derivative, construct the smooth Reeb field and the contact Hamiltonian field, and prove their flow statements with the required compactness/completeness hypotheses. Distinguish forms from distributions, cooriented from unoriented data and strict from conformal contact maps. Build the actual symplectization and normalized standard/sphere/ellipsoid examples.

## SC.2: Contact normal forms and isotopy

Prove contact Darboux, compact Gray stability with a positive conformal multiplier, and the neighbourhood theorem for a compact boundaryless embedded Legendrian using J^1L. Import generic tubular neighbourhoods and flows. Do not strengthen Gray stability to strict preservation of the contact forms.

## SC.3: Lagrangian neighbourhoods and embeddings

Import the existing cotangent, symplectic and Lagrangian objects. Prove Weinstein neighbourhoods for compact boundaryless embedded Lagrangians, graph/closed-one-form and exact-primitive comparisons, and the symplectic-normal-bundle neighbourhood theorem. Keep generic relative Moser with its owner and exact Floer theory in HeegaardFloer.

## SC.4: Hamiltonian actions and moment maps

Build smooth group actions, actual fundamental fields and coadjoint-equivariant moment maps using the stated signs and period lattice. Prove conservation, connected-manifold uniqueness up to an invariant constant, and cotangent/product constructions. Component Hamiltonians alone do not establish equivariance.

## SC.5: Regular symplectic reduction

For compact free Hamiltonian actions at a nonempty zero level, construct the actual quotient and reduced form, prove its closedness/nondegeneracy, and prove qualified reduction in stages and reduced dynamics. Locally free and singular levels are not silently treated as smooth manifold quotients. Compute the projective-space reduction with its area normalization.

## SC.6: Hamiltonian tori and convexity

Prove connected moment fibers and convexity on compact connected manifolds, using actual equivariant normal forms and the Morse-Bott handle/level-set inputs. Do not substitute isolated-critical-point Morse theory. Track the torus lattice, fixed components and effective dimension bound.

## SC.7: Delzant construction and classification

Construct toric manifolds from simple rational smooth polytopes with real support constants, using their lattice maps and regular reductions. Prove equivariant moment-preserving symplectic uniqueness for a fixed torus and chosen moment map. The smooth comparison in Delzant Theorem 2.1 and the symplectic upgrade in Proposition 4.1 are separate proof phases. Translations and integral torus reidentifications require explicit changes of data; vertices need not be integral.

## Sources and proof boundaries

Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry (author revision January 2006); Geiges, Contact geometry (arXiv v2); Delzant, Hamiltoniens periodiques et images convexes de l'application moment (1988). The packet records the exact passages inspected and remaining source work. Cannas da Silva's toric chapter supplies the existence direction, not a complete uniqueness proof. The reduction slice argument and Morse-Bott convexity ingredients require their own proof closure.

stages.title: Pointwise contact and Reeb geometry
stages.description: On existing real vector spaces and bilinear forms define the contact predicate alpha nonzero, beta alternating and beta restricted to ker(alpha) nondegenerate. Package the horizontal form in the existing SymplecticForm carrier. In finite dimension construct and characterize the normalized Reeb vector, its horizontal projection and direct-product splitting. Prove naturality under linear equivalence. For first-order rescaling (c,ell), retain beta_prime=c beta+ell wedge alpha and prove the Reeb correction c^(-1)r+c^(-2)Z with beta(Z,-)=ell on the kernel. Construct the pointwise symplectization on R times V with the dt wedge alpha sign. This layer is pointwise: it does not assert that arbitrary beta equals the derivative of a given smooth alpha. Reuse the baseline dual equivalence instead of rebuilding symplectic linear algebra.

stages.title: Smooth contact forms and Reeb dynamics
stages.description: On finite-dimensional smooth real manifolds without boundary, use the actual smooth one-form alpha and its exterior derivative to impose contactness at each tangent space; prove the equivalent nonvanishing volume criterion in dimension 2n+1. Keep a selected coorientation and its global form explicit. Use SC.0 to construct a smooth Reeb vector field, proving smooth dependence through the restricted nondegenerate bundle map, and its local flow. Prove global existence under compactness or a separately stated completeness hypothesis, not for every Reeb field. Distinguish strict maps from contactomorphisms and prove the nonconstant rescaling formula for nowhere-zero functions; positive functions preserve the chosen coorientation. Pin contact Hamiltonians by alpha(X_H)=H and contraction of d alpha with X_H=(R H)alpha-dH. Construct the actual exact symplectic form d(exp(t)alpha) on R times M and its Liouville vector. Compute dz-sum p_i dq_i, the standard sphere and diagonal ellipsoids, including orbit periods under the displayed normalization. Import smooth symplectic forms, exterior calculus and flows rather than substitute formal tangent data.

stages.title: Contact normal forms and isotopy
stages.description: Prove contact Darboux in every odd real dimension using the selected form convention dz-sum p_i dq_i. For a smooth family of cooriented contact structures on a compact boundaryless manifold, prove Gray stability by an isotopy with pullback alpha_t=f_t alpha_0 and f_t positive. Do not strengthen this to preservation of the forms themselves or remove the global flow hypothesis. Prove the neighbourhood theorem for a compact boundaryless embedded Legendrian using J^1L=T*L times R and its dz-lambda form; retain the zero-section identification. Prove compactly supported contact isotopy extension with its neighbourhood and support data. The generic tubular-neighbourhood, smooth-embedding, flow and relative-Moser infrastructure is imported from its owners; only the contact-specific equations and comparisons live here.

stages.title: Lagrangian neighbourhoods and embeddings
stages.description: Use the existing symplectic-manifold, cotangent-form and Lagrangian notions. Prove the Weinstein neighbourhood theorem for a compact boundaryless embedded Lagrangian L, with a symplectomorphism between neighbourhoods of its image and of the zero section in T*L respecting that section. Fix lambda_can at a covector by evaluation on the projection differential and omega_can=-d lambda_can. A graph of a smooth one-form is Lagrangian precisely when that form is closed; with a chosen global primitive its graph is exact. Local primitives must not be confused with a global exactness statement. Prove the symplectic-neighbourhood comparison for compact boundaryless symplectic submanifolds with a specified isomorphism of their symplectic normal bundles, and the graph/diagonal test for symplectomorphisms. Reuse Darboux, relative Moser and tubular neighbourhoods. Maslov theory, holomorphic curves and the exact Lagrangian Floer complex remain with HeegaardFloer.

stages.title: Hamiltonian actions and moment maps
stages.description: For smooth actions of finite-dimensional real Lie groups on a symplectic manifold, use the actual Lie algebra, exponential and adjoint action. Reuse Hamiltonian fields and flows from the common symplectic substrate. Fix contraction i_XH omega=dH and the bracket {F,G}=omega(X_F,X_G); then X_H(F)={F,H} and [X_F,X_G]=-X_{ {F,G} }. For a left action set xi_M=d/dt at zero of exp(t xi) acting on x. A moment map satisfies d<mu,xi>=i_xi_M omega; a Hamiltonian action also requires coadjoint equivariance with Ad_(g inverse). Existence of component Hamiltonians alone does not imply equivariance. Prove Noether conservation for invariant Hamiltonians, uniqueness of moment maps on a connected manifold up to a coadjoint-invariant constant, cotangent-lift and product constructions. Normalize the circle as R/(2 pi Z): its counterclockwise action on C with dx wedge dy has moment -|z|^2/2. Track all sign and period conversions against the chosen suppliers.

stages.title: Regular symplectic reduction
stages.description: For a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly with equivariant moment map, assume the zero level is nonempty and the action on it is free. Prove regularity, construct its smooth principal quotient through the generic smooth-quotient interface, and define the unique reduced closed two-form whose pullback is the restricted original form. Prove nondegeneracy by the tangent quotient and the orbit/symplectic-orthogonal identities. Locally free actions produce orbifold issues, not a manifold theorem with the word free omitted. State other moment levels using their stabilizers and the needed regular/free hypotheses separately. Prove reduction in stages for commuting compact actions with both stage quotients free and regular, and compatibility of reduced invariant Hamiltonian flows. Compute the scalar circle reduction of C^(n+1) at moment -c, c>0, including the quotient CP^n and the convention that a projective line has area 2 pi c. The general free proper quotient theorem must be provided, not inferred from the existence of G/H for a closed subgroup.

stages.title: Hamiltonian tori and convexity
stages.description: For a compact connected symplectic manifold with a Hamiltonian torus action, prove that moment fibers are connected and the image is the convex hull of the images of the fixed-point components. Build the equivariant local normal form and weight decomposition used by the proof. Component Hamiltonians have Morse-Bott critical sets with even index and coindex; give the handle/level-set topology needed to turn those properties into connectedness rather than cite isolated-point Morse theory as sufficient. State the effective-action dimension bound, isotropic orbits, and the full-dimensional polytope conclusion in the toric case. Fixed components need not be isolated for a general Hamiltonian torus action. Keep the integral lattice and the chosen period normalization fixed; generic convex-set facts and Lie-group representations are imported from their existing theories.

stages.title: Delzant construction and classification
stages.description: Classify compact connected 2n-dimensional symplectic manifolds with effective Hamiltonian action of a fixed n-torus and a chosen moment map by their Delzant moment polytopes. The polytope is simple, rational and smooth: the primitive edge or facet-normal data at each vertex are unimodular in the fixed lattice. Support constants are real; vertices are not required to be integral. Construct the manifold by symplectic reduction of C^d using the actual lattice homomorphism and kernel torus, proving freeness from unimodularity, compactness and the exact image. Prove that two such spaces with the same normalized moment polytope are equivariantly symplectomorphic preserving the moment map. Translation enters only when forgetting its additive normalization; integral linear changes enter only with an explicit torus reidentification. Delzant Theorem 2.1 gives the smooth equivariant comparison and Proposition 4.1 provides the symplectic upgrade: both proof phases are targets. Build neither a second generic polytope library nor algebraic toric varieties, and retain the symplectic conclusion rather than stopping at diffeomorphism.
